questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are TRUE for
the Refuse-Derived Fuel (RDF) in the context of
Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) management?

options.A:
Higher Heating Value (HHV) of the unprocessed
MSW is higher than the HHV of RDF processed
from the same MSW.
options.B: RDF can be made in the powdered form
options.C:
Inorganic fraction of MSW is mostly converted
to RDF.
options.D: RDF cannot be used in conjunction with oil.

questions.explanation: (A) is false. The Higher Heating Value (HHV) of Refuse-Derived Fuel (RDF) processed from Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) is typically higher than the HHV of unprocessed MSW. This is because RDF processing removes non-combustible materials from MSW and concentrates the combustible fraction. (B) is true. RDF can be produced in various forms including pellets, fluff, and powdered form. The form of RDF depends on the specific process and intended end use. (C) is partially true. RDF processing typically removes a significant portion of the inorganic fraction of MSW, but not all of it. The remaining inorganic fraction is typically mixed with the RDF product. (D) is false. RDF can be used as a fuel in a variety of combustion systems, including those that burn oil. In fact, RDF is often used as a supplemental fuel in cement kilns and other industrial processes that also use oil as a fuel.
questions.explanation_html:
(A) is false. The Higher Heating Value (HHV) of Refuse-Derived Fuel (RDF) processed from Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) is typically higher than the HHV of unprocessed MSW. This is because RDF processing removes non-combustible materials from MSW and concentrates the combustible fraction.

(B) is true. RDF can be produced in various forms including pellets, fluff, and powdered form. The form of RDF depends on the specific process and intended end use.

(C) is partially true. RDF processing typically removes a significant portion of the inorganic fraction of MSW, but not all of it. The remaining inorganic fraction is typically mixed with the RDF product.

questions.question:

[/latex] is solved by employing a backward differnce scheme within the finite difference framework. Eulers backward difference scheme
[latex]\begin{aligned} u_{n}-u_{n-1} & =h f\left(t_{n}, u_{n}\right)=h\left(1-2 t_{n} u n^{2}\right) \\ & =0.01\left(1-2 \times 3.14 \times 1.75^{2}\right) \\ & =-0.1822 \end{aligned}[/latex]

Hence, options (A), (B) and (D) are true.

questions.question: The steady-state temperature distribution in a square plate [latex]A B C D[/latex] is governed by the 2-dimensional Laplace equation. The side [latex]A B[/latex] is kept at a temperature of [latex]100{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}[/latex] and the other three sides are kept at a temperature of [latex]0{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}[/latex]. Ignoring the effect of discontinuities in the boundary conditions at the corners, the steady-state temperature at the center of the plate is obtained as  [latex]T_0 ^{\circ} \mathrm{C}[/latex]. Due to symmetry, the steady-state temperature at the center will be same [latex]\left(\mathrm{T_0}{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\right)[/latex], when any one side of the square is kept at a temperature of [latex]100{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}[/latex] and the remaining three sides are kept at a temperature of [latex]0{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}[/latex]. Using the principle of superposition, the value of [latex]T_0[/latex] is ___ (rounded off to two decimal places).
questions.explanation:
We know, Laplace equation in two dimensional on a unit square with Dirichlet boundary condition : [latex]
\frac{\partial^{2} u}{\partial x^{2}}+\frac{\partial^{2} u}{\partial y^{2}}=0, \quad 0 \lt (x, y) \lt 1
[/latex] This Laplace equation is called harmonic function. Solution of Laplace equation, [latex]u(x, y)=\left(C_{1} \cos \beta x+C_{2} \sin \beta x\right)\left(C_{3} e^{\text {By }}+C_{4} e^{-\beta y}\right)[/latex] Let square [latex]A B C D[/latex] is unit square. Now, given [latex]
\begin{aligned}
& u(x, 0)=0 \\
& u(0, y)=0 \\
& u(1, y)=0 \\
& u(x, 1)=100
\end{aligned}
[/latex] For [latex]u(x, 0)=0[/latex] [latex]\quad 0=\left(C_{1} \cos \beta x+0\right)(C_3+C_4)[/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{C}_{3}=-\mathrm{C}_{4}[/latex] For [latex]u(0, y)=0[/latex]; [latex]0=\left(C_{1}+0\right)\left(C_{3} e^{\beta y}+C_{4} e^{-\beta y}\right)[/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{C}_{1}=0[/latex] Now, [latex]
\begin{aligned}
u(x, y) & =0+C_{2} \sin \beta x\left(C_{3} e^{\beta y}+C_{4} e^{-\beta y}\right) \\
& =a_{x} \sin \beta x\left(e^{\beta y}-e^{-\beta y}\right) \quad ...(1)
\end{aligned}
[/latex] [latex]\left[\because \mathrm{C}_{3}=-\mathrm{C}_{4}\right.[/latex] and Let [latex]\left.\mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{C}_{3}=\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{x}}\right][/latex] For [latex]u(1, y)=0[/latex] [latex]
0=a_{x} \sin \beta x\left(e^{\beta y}-e^{\beta y}\right)
[/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow \quad \beta=\mathrm{n} \pi[/latex] For [latex]u(x, 1)=100[/latex] [latex]a_{x} \sin n\pi x\left(e^{n\pi}-e^{-n \pi}\right)=100[/latex] [latex]
a_{x}=\frac{100}{\sin n\pi x\left(e^{n\pi}-e^{-n \pi}\right)}
[/latex] From eqn. (1), we get [latex]
\begin{gathered}
u(x, y)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{100}{\sin n \pi x\left(e^{n\pi}-e^{-n\pi}\right)} \times \sin n\pi x\left(e^{n \pi y}-e^{- n\pi y}\right) \\
=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{100}{\left(e^{n\pi}-e^{-n \pi}\right)}\left[e^{n\pi y}-e^{-n\pi y}\right]
\end{gathered}
[/latex] Now, at mid point [latex](x, y)=\left(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{2}\right)[/latex] [latex] u\left(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{2}\right)=T_{0} \text { [given] } [/latex] [latex]
\begin{aligned}
T_0&=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{100}{\left(\mathrm{e}^{n\pi}-\mathrm{e}^{-n\pi}\right)}\left[\mathrm{e}^{n\pi / 2}-\mathrm{e}^{-n\pi / 2}\right] \\
&=100\left [ \left ( \frac{\mathrm{e}^{\pi / 2}-\mathrm{e}^{-\pi / 2}}{\mathrm{e}^{\pi}-\mathrm{e}^{-\pi}} \right )  +\left ( \frac{\mathrm{e}^{\pi}-\mathrm{e}^{-\pi}}{\mathrm{e}^{2\pi}-\mathrm{e}^{-2\pi}} \right )+...\right ]\\
&=100\left [ \frac{1}{(\mathrm{e}^{\pi / 2}-\mathrm{e}^{-\pi / 2})}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{e}^{\pi}-\mathrm{e}^{-\pi}}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{e}^{3\pi / 2}-\mathrm{e}^{-3\pi / 2}} +...(neglect) \right ]\\
&=100[0.199+0.043+0.008]\\
&\approx 25^{\circ}C
\end{aligned}
[/latex]

options.D: calcium and magnesium increase hardness and total dissolved solids

questions.explanation: Total dissolved solids comprise of inorganic salts, principally calcium, magnesium, potassium, sodium bicarbonates, chlorides, sulfates and some small amount of organic matter that are dissolved in water. Hardness is due to presence of multivalent cations. In most cases, it is due to the presence of soluble bicarbonates, chlorides and sulfates of calcium and magnesium. Presence of particulate matter decreases the effectiveness of UV disinfection or chlorine disinfection by shielding the targeted microorganisms.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is/are TRUE for the aerobic composting of sewage sludge?

options.A: Bulking agent is added during the composting process to reduce the porosity of the solid mixture
options.B: Leachate can be generated during composting
options.C: Actinomycetes are involved in the process
options.D: In-vessel composting systems cannot be operated in the plug-flow mode

questions.explanation:
A bulking agent (wood ships shredded leaves or types) is intended to support the structure of sludge by increasing its porosity to encourage effective aeration. In-vessel composting systems can be divided into plug flow and agitated bed modes. In plug flow mode, the relationship between particles in the composting mass stays the same through the process and the system operates on first-in, first-out principle. In an agitated bed system, composting material is mixed mechanically during the processing. The heat produced in aquatic composting cause any surplus moisture to be extracted as water vapour and hence no leachate is produced. Actinomycetes are aerobic, spore forming positive bacteria. These are thermophilic species and their development depends on aerobic conditions, temperature and water content. The heat produced in aerobic
composting helps support the growth of these species. Leachate can generated from vegetable wastes.

Given: Diffusion equation:
[latex] \frac{\partial T}{\partial t}=\mathrm{D} \frac{\partial^{2} \mathrm{~T}}{\partial \mathrm{x}^{2}} [/latex]
And also,
[latex]D=1[/latex]
[latex]\mathrm{T}(0, \mathrm{t})=0[/latex]
[latex]\mathrm{T}(5,5)=0[/latex]
[latex]T(x, 0)=T_{0}[/latex]
We know, solution of equation is given by,
[latex]T(x, t)=\left(C_{1} \cos \alpha x+C_{2} \sin \alpha x\right) C_{3} e^{-\alpha^{2} t} \;\;\; ...(1)[/latex]

For [latex]\mathrm{T}(0, t)=0[/latex]
[latex]\left(C_{1}+0\right) C_{3} e^{-\alpha^{2} t}=0[/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow \mathrm{C}_{1}=0[/latex]

For [latex]\mathrm{T}(\mathrm{s}, \mathrm{t})=0[/latex]
[latex]\left(C_{2} \sin \alpha 5\right) C_{3} \mathrm{e}^{-25 t}=0[/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow \sin 5 \alpha=0[/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow \alpha=\frac{\mathrm{n} \pi}{5}[/latex]

Now, from equation (1)
[latex]T(x, t)=C_{2} C_{3} \sin \left(\frac{n \pi x}{5}\right) e^{-\frac{n^{2} \pi^{2}}{25} t}[/latex]
[latex]=b_{n} \sin \left(\frac{n \pi x}{5}\right) e^{-\frac{n^{2} \pi^{2} t}{25}}[/latex]

Generalize solution
[latex]T(x, t)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} b_{n} \sin \left(\frac{n \pi x}{5}\right) e^{-\frac{n^{2} \pi^{2} t}{25}}[/latex]
For [latex]\mathrm{T}(\mathrm{x}, 0)=\mathrm{T}_{0}[/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow T_{0}=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} b_{n} \sin \left(\frac{n \pi x}{5}\right)[/latex]

From fourier series,
[latex]b_{n}=0[/latex] for even value of [latex]n[/latex]
[latex]\therefore \mathrm{T}(\mathrm{x}, \mathrm{t})=\sum_{\mathrm{n}=13,5 \ldots .}^{\infty} \mathrm{b}_{\mathrm{n}} \sin \left(\frac{\mathrm{n} \pi \mathrm{x}}{5}\right) \mathrm{e}^{-\frac{\mathrm{n}^{2} \pi^{2} \mathrm{t}}{25}}[/latex]

Given: [latex]T(x, t)=\sum_{n=13,5 \ldots .}^{\infty} C_{n} \sin \left(\frac{n \pi x}{5}\right) e^{-\beta n^{2} t}[/latex]
On comparison;
[latex]\beta=\frac{\pi^{2}}{25}=0.395 \mathrm{sec}^{-1}[/latex]

\frac{\partial^{2} u}{\partial x^{2}}+\frac{\partial^{2} u}{\partial y^{2}}=0, \quad 0 \lt (x, y) \lt 1

\begin{aligned}
& u(x, 0)=0 \\
& u(0, y)=0 \\
& u(1, y)=0 \\
& u(x, 1)=100
\end{aligned}
[/latex] For [latex]u(x, 0)=0[/latex] [latex]\quad 0=\left(C_{1} \cos \beta x+0\right)(C_3+C_4)[/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{C}_{3}=-\mathrm{C}_{4}[/latex] For [latex]u(0, y)=0[/latex]; [latex]0=\left(C_{1}+0\right)\left(C_{3} e^{\beta y}+C_{4} e^{-\beta y}\right)[/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{C}_{1}=0[/latex] Now, [latex]
\begin{aligned}
u(x, y) & =0+C_{2} \sin \beta x\left(C_{3} e^{\beta y}+C_{4} e^{-\beta y}\right) \\

questions.explanation_html:
Given: Diffusion equation:
[latex] \frac{\partial T}{\partial t}=\mathrm{D} \frac{\partial^{2} \mathrm{~T}}{\partial \mathrm{x}^{2}} [/latex]
And also,
[latex]D=1[/latex]
[latex]\mathrm{T}(0, \mathrm{t})=0[/latex]
[latex]\mathrm{T}(5,5)=0[/latex]
[latex]T(x, 0)=T_{0}[/latex]
We know, solution of equation is given by,
[latex]T(x, t)=\left(C_{1} \cos \alpha x+C_{2} \sin \alpha x\right) C_{3} e^{-\alpha^{2} t} \;\;\; ...(1)[/latex]

For [latex]\mathrm{T}(0, t)=0[/latex]
[latex]\left(C_{1}+0\right) C_{3} e^{-\alpha^{2} t}=0[/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow \mathrm{C}_{1}=0[/latex]

For [latex]\mathrm{T}(\mathrm{s}, \mathrm{t})=0[/latex]
[latex]\left(C_{2} \sin \alpha 5\right) C_{3} \mathrm{e}^{-25 t}=0[/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow \sin 5 \alpha=0[/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow \alpha=\frac{\mathrm{n} \pi}{5}[/latex]

Now, from equation (1)
[latex]T(x, t)=C_{2} C_{3} \sin \left(\frac{n \pi x}{5}\right) e^{-\frac{n^{2} \pi^{2}}{25} t}[/latex]
[latex]=b_{n} \sin \left(\frac{n \pi x}{5}\right) e^{-\frac{n^{2} \pi^{2} t}{25}}[/latex]

Generalize solution
[latex]T(x, t)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} b_{n} \sin \left(\frac{n \pi x}{5}\right) e^{-\frac{n^{2} \pi^{2} t}{25}}[/latex]

[latex]\Rightarrow T_{0}=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} b_{n} \sin \left(\frac{n \pi x}{5}\right)[/latex]

From fourier series,
[latex]b_{n}=0[/latex] for even value of [latex]n[/latex]
[latex]\therefore \mathrm{T}(\mathrm{x}, \mathrm{t})=\sum_{\mathrm{n}=13,5 \ldots .}^{\infty} \mathrm{b}_{\mathrm{n}} \sin \left(\frac{\mathrm{n} \pi \mathrm{x}}{5}\right) \mathrm{e}^{-\frac{\mathrm{n}^{2} \pi^{2} \mathrm{t}}{25}}[/latex]

Given: [latex]T(x, t)=\sum_{n=13,5 \ldots .}^{\infty} C_{n} \sin \left(\frac{n \pi x}{5}\right) e^{-\beta n^{2} t}[/latex]
On comparison;
[latex]\beta=\frac{\pi^{2}}{25}=0.395 \mathrm{sec}^{-1}[/latex]
